Rumor: Nintendo to Drop Optical Storage for NX

fresh speculation - promoted by comments made by Macronix, the company which traditionally supplies Nintendo with its ROM chips - suggests that the firm could opt to use cartridges or game cards for NX, like it does with the 3DS.

This could be pretty cool. I'm always concerned by these rumors because abandoning physical media entirely would suck; right now the Wii U is the friendliest for people with bandwidth constraints because game updates tend to be smaller than on the XB1, PS4, or PC. But forgoing discs and returning cartridges would be interesting. It could mean that game saves carry with the card instead of with the console, like how it is on the 3DS. What would be really cool is if Nintendo started applying updates to the cartridges before they go out, but the logistics of that might be difficult.
I agree, I feel the same way about a lot of things. It also draw the question that if they go for cartridges, could the system be backwards compatible with 3DS games?

That would be amazing! And it would mean that the NX could launch with an existing library of games.

It could even mean having an NX console and an NX portable that all run the same games, since they couldn't do that with discs before. It all depends on how much a handheld version would handle, but they could also leave that door open and release a handheld NX as the technology catches up with the console. It would be quite a hat-trick since it's something that Sony and Microsoft's disc-based consoles wouldn't be able to mimic.

I like your thinking, it could really set them apart. The more I think about this idea the more I like it. I'm trying to keep my hopes at a low because I don't want to be let down but these are some pretty great ideas.

Thanks! I also try not to get my hopes up, but it's interesting to think about where the industry might go :) it's encouraging to realize that Nintendo has some options at making a comeback; all that's left is to see if they take them.

One of the supposedly "highly reliable sourced" leaks said that the NX will be cartridge based and use three types of cartridges. One is NX only, one is handheld only, and one will work on both. That way if a developer wants to focus only on one experience (console or handheld), they can.

That is an interesting approach. On the one hand it solves the problem of one system being more powerful than the other, but introduces its own complications - potentially three versions of a game. It might end up being the best fit solution anyway.

Well you wouldn't have multiple versions of a game, just one. If the developer wants to spend the time making the game work on both systems, then they just put it on the cartridge that works on both systems. Like how all Gameboy games worked on Gameboy Color (but Gameboy Color games wouldn't work on a Gameboy) and there were also black cartridges that would work on both systems. So Nintendo has done this before, but with less drastic differences in hardware.
That's a good point. It would also be nice to buy one game and have it run on both systems even if the handheld system scales the graphics back - similar to Super Smash Bros on the Wii U and 3DS.
Definitely. If they do use cartridges, I hope that they allow games to download DLC / updates directly to the cartridge so you take the updates to any system you plug them in to.

I think that's a great idea, and maximizes the benefits of having gameplay media that doubles as storage. They could also apply updates before they ship a game, for example: Team Fortress 2 can be purchased on physical media, but the game has grown significantly from its original ~2GB file size that you can still get on disc. It would be nice if every time a game shipped - even just to vendors - it was patched to the current version. That would mean that when you receive a game, there's a good chance it's at least part of the way up to date - less data to download and less time between receiving a game and it being ready to play.

It would also allow Nintendo to state that they're better for buying all of your games (even multiplatform games) because, due to updates / DLC being stored on the cartridge, you never have to worry about losing content when the servers eventually go down.
This could also improve loading times, god I hate that WiiU startup loading screen shenanigans. Most N64 games had virtually no loading screens, those where nice times.
